title: Timeout does not cancel work
lesson: A read can finish remotely after its caller times out; a bounded retry waits, then makes a new attempt.

transcript.text: A normal read receives a response before the attempt timeout. The caller accepts it.
A separate read starts at 7s. The caller waits three seconds, then times out while the service keeps working.
During a sampled 4.5-second backoff, the service completes at 12s. Its late response arrives at 13.2s and is rejected by the expired attempt. Timeout did not cancel the work.
The delay indicator clears and the caller uses the second and final permitted attempt. This read succeeds.

The accepted result and two-attempt limit hold, then fade to black. This cut illustrates per-attempt waiting and late responses; it does not show an overall deadline, retry exhaustion, or fleet-level jitter.

changes: Shortened sampled backoff from six to 4.5 seconds, preserving the late response and its rejection.
Enlarged states, packet chips, attempt count, and bar labels for 350px viewing.
Cleared stale server success before retry, and removed the completed delay indicator.
Retimed transcript and added explicit scope limits.
Made the fade cover the entire frame, including title, so the exact encoded first and last frames match.
Moved the attempt-limit caption above its counter to keep enlarged moving request chips clear.

limitations: Read-only request; write safety requires documented idempotency or reconciliation.
Per-attempt timeout and a two-attempt limit are shown; operation-wide deadline and retry exhaustion are not.
One sampled delay does not demonstrate fleet-level jitter. Timing is illustrative.
